observations.detail: Added TokenBlacklist class (src/auth/token-blacklist.ts) using an in-memory Map<token, expiresAt> with automatic pruning of expired entries. In production this should be replaced by a Redis set with TTL. The blacklist integrates into auth middleware as an optional parameter to avoid breaking existing callers.

Implemented refresh token rotation: the refresh endpoint blacklists the old refresh token before issuing a new pair. This limits a stolen refresh token to single use. The blacklist is shared between the routes and middleware layers via dependency injection.

Strengthened password validation to require uppercase + lowercase + digit in addition to the 8-char minimum. Used simple regex checks (/[A-Z]/, /[a-z]/, /[0-9]/) rather than a library like zxcvbn to keep the implementation lightweight and dependency-free.

Replaced Math.random()-based hex ID generation in UserStore with crypto.randomUUID(). The global crypto object is available in Node.js ≥ 19 and all modern runtimes without importing node:crypto. This avoids the ESM dynamic import pattern used elsewhere in the codebase.

The auth middleware's blacklist parameter is optional (TokenBlacklistChecker | undefined) so the middleware remains backward-compatible with callers that don't need blacklisting. Existing tests that don't pass a blacklist continue to work unchanged.

When updating password complexity requirements, all test passwords must be updated to satisfy the new rules. Tests that previously used 'password123' (no uppercase) needed to change to 'Password123'. The password-without-uppercase and password-without-digit test cases verify the new validation explicitly.

All 47 tests pass (up from 40). New tests cover: password without uppercase rejected, password without digit rejected, refresh token rotation (reuse rejected), TokenBlacklist add/has, TokenBlacklist expired entry pruning, and auth middleware blacklisted token rejection. PR #7 opened against feature/jwt-authentication.
